## Introduction


If you want to increase subscription signups on Shopify, a bigger subscribe-and-save discount is a weak lever. It costs margin on the first order and on every renewal after it.


It also tells shoppers the price was never the real price. That's a hard lesson to unteach.


Shoppers subscribe for better reasons than a few points off. Convenience, control, and a first order that feels like a win.


This guide covers six offers that give them one of those reasons. We're[Playably](https://playably.ai/) , so one of the six is ours: a gamified rebate where shoppers pay full price and can win 100% of their order back.


We'll show what that rebate did to Soul CBD's subscription rate, then where the other five fit and how to pick.


### Key Takeaways


- A deeper subscribe discount costs margin on every renewal, not just the first order.
- 59% of Soul CBD campaign buyers subscribed, against 41% of other shoppers.
- Playably helps increase subscription signups on Shopify without cutting the subscription price.
- Brand-new Soul CBD customers subscribed at 54%, against 36% of other first-time buyers.
- Skip and pause controls answer the fear of being locked in.


## Why a Bigger Subscribe Discount Is a Weak Lever


The usual fix for a flat subscription rate is a deeper discount, with ten percent becoming 15, then 20.


Each step is paid again on every renewal for as long as the subscription runs. The cost compounds while the reason to subscribe stays the same.


It also anchors the product's value to a markdown. A shopper who joined for the discount is watching the discount, which is how[discount fatigue](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/discount-fatigue) sets in.


The six offers below give shoppers a reason to subscribe that isn't the price. Most of them protect your margin.


One of them, run by Playably, holds full price on the first order as well.


## 1. A Conditional Cashback Rebate on the Order


This is the one with a published result behind it.


Soul CBD ran a Playably campaign called OVERTIME Big Game Cashback, from January 26 to February 7, 2026. Shoppers bought at full price and were auto-entered for a chance to get 100% of their order back if the trigger hit.


The subscription numbers are the part to study. 59% of campaign buyers subscribed, compared with 41% of other shoppers that same week, which is 1.4× the subscription sign-up rate.


New customers moved too. Brand-new customers subscribed at 1.5× the rate of other first-time buyers, 54% against 36%.


The subscribers stayed. 63% renewed at least once, close to the 67% renewal rate of Soul's regular subscribers.


Baskets grew as well. They ran 16% bigger than the rest of the store, $99 against $86.


The shopper pays the real price, and the reward on the table is the whole order rather than a few dollars off it. Playably insures and hedges the payout, so the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps full margin.


You can see the live[Soul campaign page](https://playably.ai/pages/soul) on[playably.ai](http://playably.ai/) .


## 2. A Gift With the First Subscription Box


A small add-on in the first box gives shoppers something to unbox that a one-time order doesn't get. A sample of a second product, an accessory, a refill.


The cost shape is the point. You pay for one gift, once, instead of a percentage off every renewal.


Pick a gift that makes the core product easier to use or introduces the next thing they might buy. That second job helps you[increase average order value](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/increase-average-order-value) later.


Keep the gift on the product page, right beside the subscribe option. A gift the shopper finds out about at checkout does less work.


## 3. Skip, Swap and Pause Controls, Shown Up Front


Some shoppers stall at the subscribe button because they picture a cancellation maze.


Show the controls before they commit. One line under the subscribe option, such as "Skip, swap or pause any time," answers the question at the moment it comes up.


Then honour it. Make skipping a delivery a one-tap job in the account area and in the reminder email.


A paused subscriber is still a subscriber you can bring back. When they lapse, a[win-back without discounts](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/win-back-customers-without-discounts) brings them home without teaching them to wait for a code.


## 4. A Quiz That Matches the Product and the Cadence


If shoppers aren't sure which product or which frequency is right, a short quiz settles both.


Ask what they use, how often, and what they want to change. Then recommend a product and a delivery interval, with the subscribe option already selected.


Playably builds this kind of test. The[Tier 1 build fee](https://playably.ai/products/tier-1-build-fee) covers a gamified email and landing page test with a quiz designed to improve engagement, capture email leads and drive conversions.


It comes with a dedicated brand strategist. The published price is a one time build fee of about $1,500, plus a 15% revenue share on transactions generated through the gamified experience.


## 5. Members-Only Access for Subscribers


Give subscribers something one-time buyers can't get. Early access to a new flavour, a limited colourway, first pick of a restock.


Access costs you very little. It turns the subscription into membership, which is a reason to stay that has nothing to do with price.


Name the perk on the product page and in the post-purchase email. Then deliver on it at least once in the first few billing cycles, so the promise feels real.


If you already run points or tiers, this fits inside them. Our guide to[gamified loyalty program strategies](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/gamification-strategies-for-loyalty-programs-keeping-customers-coming-back) covers how to layer perks without stacking discounts.


## 6. Free Shipping on Subscription Orders


Free shipping on recurring orders is the plainest perk on this list.


It still costs money. Shipping is a real line on every renewal, just like a discount.


Treat it like any other markdown and run the numbers before you commit. Our breakdown of[cashback versus discount code math](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/cash-back-vs-discount-codes) shows how to compare the cost of each.


Free shipping works best paired with one of the other five. It removes a small objection while the bigger reason to subscribe does the selling.

If subscription rate is the number you report on, start with the rebate, because it's the only option here with a published subscription result.


If shoppers say they're unsure what to order, start with the quiz. If they say they're scared of commitment, start with the controls.

## Conclusion


The fastest way to increase subscription signups on Shopify isn't a deeper subscribe discount. It's a better reason to subscribe.


Gifts, controls, quizzes, perks and free shipping each answer a different hesitation. A conditional cashback rebate turns the first order into a chance to win it all back, while the price stays where it is.
